scientific_intent.precision_sensitivity: Float32 concentration/scratch/coefficients, independent Float64 operator using actualF32 initial values and parameters. scientific_intent.community_use_case: Gray–Scott is a reaction-diffusion pattern-formation model. The source provides a finite numerical operator, not a calibrated chemical experiment; domain users need boundary, timestep, positivity and discretization checks beyond agreement of min/max statistics.
scientific_intent.description: Historical Julia genuinely implemented zero-flux Gray–Scott mathematics but fused every timestep into one kernel with a different random-input generator. Current versions restore the original staged pencil pipeline so timing compares the same algorithm and buffers.
scientific_intent.provenance: Native main.cu kinetic parameters and pipeline, kernels.cu Gray–Scott/axis derivatives/Laplacian/Euler update, util.h central cube generator. Standard equation identity follows the explicit source rate expressions; no application experiment or primary paper inferred.
